lead: A singly reinforced section stops at M<sub>u,lim</sub>: more tension steel would only make it over-reinforced. When the moment is larger and the depth is fixed by headroom, steel is also placed near the compression face. That compression steel A<sub>sc</sub>, together with an equal force of extra tension steel A<sub>st2</sub>, forms a second couple that carries the moment above M<sub>u,lim</sub> while the concrete block stays at x<sub>u,max</sub>. Beams at supports of continuous frames and in earthquake frames are doubly reinforced.
prereq: You need singly reinforced beams and the limit xu,max from balanced and over-reinforced sections.

blocks.text: Part 1 is the singly reinforced beam at its limit: block at x<sub>u,max</sub>, steel A<sub>st,lim</sub>, moment M<sub>u,lim</sub>. Part 2 is a steel couple: compression steel A<sub>sc</sub> at depth d′ balanced by extra tension steel A<sub>st2</sub>, with lever arm d − d′, carrying M<sub>u</sub> − M<sub>u,lim</sub>.

M<sub>u</sub> − M<sub>u,lim</sub> = f<sub>sc</sub> A<sub>sc</sub> (d − d′)     0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st2</sub> = f<sub>sc</sub> A<sub>sc</sub>     A<sub>st</sub> = A<sub>st,lim</sub> + A<sub>st2</sub>
blocks.where: f<sub>sc</sub> is the design stress in the compression steel (Annex G-1.2), in N/mm².

blocks.text: Some textbooks write the steel force as (f<sub>sc</sub> − 0.446 f<sub>ck</sub>) A<sub>sc</sub> to subtract the displaced concrete; that raises A<sub>sc</sub> a few per cent. This book uses the Annex G form.

sections.h3: The stress in the compression steel

blocks.text: The compression steel strain is less than the 0.0035 at the top:

blocks.where: f<sub>sc</sub> is then read from the design stress-strain curve of the bar.

blocks.text: For Fe250 (mild steel, elastic then flat) f<sub>sc</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> = 217.5 N/mm² once ε<sub>sc</sub> ≥ 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>/E<sub>s</sub> = 0.00109. Fe415 and Fe500 are cold-worked bars with a curved design diagram (IS 456 Fig. 23A): the stress is linear up to 0.8 × 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> and reaches 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> only at a strain of 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>/E<sub>s</sub> + 0.002. For Fe415 that strain is 0.0038, more than the compression steel ever gets, so f<sub>sc</sub> is below 361 N/mm². SP 16 Table F lists the result against d′/d:

items: Design: compute M<sub>u,lim</sub>. If M<sub>u</sub> ≤ M<sub>u,lim</sub>, design a singly reinforced section instead.
Set x<sub>u</sub> = x<sub>u,max</sub> and find ε<sub>sc</sub> = 0.0035(x<sub>u,max</sub> − d′)/x<sub>u,max</sub>; read f<sub>sc</sub> (or take it from Table F for d′/d).
A<sub>sc</sub> = (M<sub>u</sub> − M<sub>u,lim</sub>)/[f<sub>sc</sub> (d − d′)] and A<sub>st2</sub> = f<sub>sc</sub> A<sub>sc</sub>/(0.87 f<sub>y</sub>).

A<sub>st</sub> = A<sub>st,lim</sub> + A<sub>st2</sub>. Check A<sub>st</sub> and A<sub>sc</sub> are each at most 0.04 b D, choose bars, and tie the compression bars with stirrups so they cannot buckle.

Analysis of a given section: assume the tension steel yields, guess x<sub>u</sub>, find ε<sub>sc</sub> and f<sub>sc</sub>, and adjust x<sub>u</sub> until 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub> + f<sub>sc</sub> A<sub>sc</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub>. Confirm x<sub>u</sub> ≤ x<sub>u,max</sub>, then M<sub>u</sub> = 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub> (d − 0.42 x<sub>u</sub>) + f<sub>sc</sub> A<sub>sc</sub> (d − d′).

blocks.text: Compression steel also reduces long-term deflection (deflection control). When the excess moment is large, a deeper section or a flanged beam is often cheaper. The design aids tabulate pt and pc for doubly reinforced sections.

examples.question: Design a beam 250 mm wide with an effective depth of 500 mm (d′ = 50 mm) for a factored moment of 250 kN·m, using M25 concrete and Fe415 steel.
steps: M<sub>u</sub> = 250 kN·m > 215.57 kN·m, so the beam is doubly reinforced. Excess moment ΔM = 250 − 215.57 = 34.43 kN·m.
ε<sub>sc</sub> = 0.0035 × (240 − 50)/240 = 0.00277. On the Fe415 curve this lies just above (0.00276, 351.8), so f<sub>sc</sub> = 352.1 N/mm² (Table F, d′/d = 0.10: 353 N/mm²).
Provide 2 bars of 25 mm + 2 bars of 22 mm at the bottom (982 + 760 = 1742 mm²) and 2 bars of 12 mm at the top (226 mm²). With D = 550 mm, 0.04 b D = 5500 mm², well above both.
examples.answer: A<sub>sc</sub> = 217 mm² (2 bars of 12 mm) and A<sub>st</sub> = 1708 mm² (2 of 25 mm + 2 of 22 mm, 1742 mm²); f<sub>sc</sub> = 352 N/mm², not 361 N/mm².

examples.question: A beam 300 mm wide has d = 550 mm and d′ = 50 mm, with 4 bars of 25 mm in tension and 2 bars of 20 mm in compression. M20 concrete, Fe415 steel. Find its moment of resistance.
steps: A<sub>st</sub> = 1963.5 mm²; A<sub>sc</sub> = 628.3 mm². Tension, if the bars yield: T = 0.87 × 415 × 1963.5 = 708.9 kN.
Trial x<sub>u</sub> = 230 mm: ε<sub>sc</sub> = 0.00274, f<sub>sc</sub> = 351.5 N/mm²; C = 496.8 + 220.8 = 717.6 kN > 708.9 kN. So x<sub>u</sub> lies between.
Converged: x<sub>u</sub> = 226.1 mm, f<sub>sc</sub> = 351.1 N/mm²; C<sub>c</sub> = 488.3 kN, C<sub>s</sub> = 220.6 kN, total 708.9 kN.
Checks: x<sub>u,max</sub> = 0.48 × 550 = 264 mm, so x<sub>u</sub> < x<sub>u,max</sub>; tension steel strain = 0.0035 × (550 − 226.1)/226.1 = 0.0050, above 0.0038, so the bars yield as assumed.
examples.answer: x<sub>u</sub> = 226.1 mm, f<sub>sc</sub> = 351 N/mm², M<sub>u</sub> = 332.5 kN·m; without the compression bars the same tension steel would make the beam over-reinforced (M<sub>u,lim</sub> = 250.4 kN·m).

traps: Taking f<sub>sc</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> for Fe415. The curve reaches 361 N/mm² only at a strain of 0.0038; in the first example 361 N/mm² gives A<sub>sc</sub> = 211.9 mm² instead of 217.3 mm², 2.5 % unsafe.
Adding A<sub>sc</sub> without A<sub>st2</sub>. The compression bars carry force only if extra tension steel balances them; without A<sub>st2</sub> the concrete block deepens past x<sub>u,max</sub>.
Writing A<sub>st2</sub> = A<sub>sc</sub>. That is true only if f<sub>sc</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>. In the first example A<sub>st2</sub> = 211.9 mm² against A<sub>sc</sub> = 217.3 mm².

Designing with x<sub>u</sub> below x<sub>u,max</sub> when M<sub>u</sub> > M<sub>u,lim</sub>. The concrete block must be used fully (x<sub>u</sub> = x<sub>u,max</sub>) before steel is added; any other x<sub>u</sub> gives a different, uneconomic answer.

A large cover to the compression steel. With d′ = 150 mm in the first example, ε<sub>sc</sub> = 0.0035 × 90/240 = 0.00131, still elastic, so f<sub>sc</sub> = 262.5 N/mm² and A<sub>sc</sub> = 34.43 × 10⁶/(262.5 × 350) = 374.8 mm².

quiz.q: What is a doubly reinforced beam?
quiz.a: A beam with designed steel near the compression face (A<sub>sc</sub>) as well as near the tension face (A<sub>st</sub>); the compression steel and extra tension steel carry the moment beyond M<sub>u,lim</sub>.

quiz.q: Why is x<sub>u</sub> taken equal to x<sub>u,max</sub> in the design of a doubly reinforced beam?
quiz.a: The concrete is then carrying the most it is allowed to (M<sub>u,lim</sub>) and the steel only has to carry the excess. A shallower block would waste concrete capacity and need more steel.

quiz.q: For b = 300 mm, d = 450 mm, d′ = 45 mm, M20 and Fe415, find M<sub>u,lim</sub> and the compression steel for M<sub>u</sub> = 200 kN·m. Use Table F.
In the first worked example, what A<sub>sc</sub> results if the cover to the compression steel is 150 mm?
In worked example 2, check what happens if the 2 bars of 20 mm at the top are ignored.
quiz.a: x<sub>u</sub> = 708.9 × 10³/(0.36 × 20 × 300) = 328.2 mm, above x<sub>u,max</sub> = 264 mm, so the section would be over-reinforced and credited only M<sub>u,lim</sub> = 250.4 kN·m. The compression bars lift it to 332.5 kN·m and keep it ductile.

beyond: Not for the exam. In earthquake frames IS 13920 requires bottom steel at each beam end of at least half the top steel, so most frame beams are doubly reinforced anyway. Compression bars need close stirrups or they buckle once the cover spalls. Search for IS 13920 beam detailing.

figure.caption: The doubly reinforced beam of the first worked example split into two couples: concrete with 1496 mm² of steel carries M<sub>u,lim</sub> = 215.57 kN·m, and 217 mm² of compression steel at 352 N/mm² with 212 mm² of extra tension steel carries the remaining 34.43 kN·m over a 450 mm arm.
